title: Let your agent draw. We make sure the diagram works.
snippet:
Invite someone with a share link. Recipients must log in; links default to View, last 30 days and are not revocable before use.

From program to teammate
Offer diagrams in your product without running a browser farm. Create a stored diagram, keep its ID for later updates, and hand an edit URL or share invitation to a teammate.

A real answer.
bash
```
curl https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/render \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $MERMAID_API_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"code": "flowchart TD\n  A[Start] --> B[Done]", "format": "svg"}' \
-o diagram.svg
```
The response is the image itself, ready to write to disk.

Mermaid API is a hosted service that runs Mermaid for you: your program sends diagram code over HTTP and gets back a validation result, an image, or new diagram code.
No. Any Mermaid account works, including a free one, and every account gets a monthly allowance of API credits. Paid plans include a bigger allowance.
Costs depend on the operation and options; stored-diagram reads are free. Your monthly allowance is spent first, then any credits you have bought. See the current costs in [api.mermaid.ai/v1/docs](https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/docs); the free balance endpoint also returns your balance and endpoint costs. For high volume, contact sales.

title: MCP Server — Mermaid Chart
snippet:
The Mermaid MCP Server supports multiple transport modes, and **every tool call requires authentication** with a Mermaid account. Authentication is free — you can sign up for a free Mermaid account (the Basic tier) to get started. Authenticate automatically via **OAuth 2.1 with Dynamic Client Registration** (for clients that support OAuth discovery, such as VS Code, Cursor, and Antigravity via `mcp-remote`), or manually by pasting a Mermaid token into your client configuration. See Authentication Setup below for details on both options.
**Available Transport Types:**
- **HTTP**: `https://mcp.mermaid.ai/mcp` with `"type": "http"`
- **SSE (Server-Sent Events)**: `https://mcp.mermaid.ai/sse` with `"type": "sse"`
**Authentication:** Every tool call requires a valid Mermaid login — free to create — either through automatic OAuth or a manually configured Authorization header.
### Available Tools
> All tools listed below require Mermaid authentication (OAuth login or a manual token). Authentication is free: a Basic Mermaid account works, no paid plan required.

Every tool call requires you to be logged in to your Mermaid account. Signing up is free — the Basic tier costs nothing. There are two ways to authenticate:
#### Option 1: OAuth Login (recommended)
If your MCP client supports OAuth discovery, no manual token setup is required. The first time you call a tool, a browser window opens asking you to log in to your Mermaid account. Once you log in, your client stays authenticated automatically — no token needs to be added to your config.
Just use the plain, header-free configuration examples above.
#### Option 2: Manual Token-Based Authentication (still supported)
1. **Get Your Token**: Visit your Mermaid account settings and generate an API token
2. **Add to Configuration**: Include the token in the `Authorization` header as shown in the examples above
3. **Replace Placeholder**: Change `YOUR_MERMAID_TOKEN_HERE` with your actual token
If the token is missing or invalid, and OAuth login hasn’t completed, **every** tool call is rejected.

title: mermaid-api.readthedocs.io/en/latest/_sources/authentication.rst.txt
snippet:
MERMAID secures its API in two ways, for two different kinds of client:
- **Writing a script, notebook, or any other code that talks to the API?** Use an `API key`_. It is the simplest option, and does not expire every few hours like a JWT does, so it is almost always what you want.
- **Building an interactive application where a person signs in through a browser?** Use `OAuth2 tokens`_ instead; an API key cannot be used to complete a browser login.
Either way, you first need a MERMAID account.
1. Create a MERMAID Account
---------------------------
Before you can request a token or an API key, you must first create a MERMAID user account. If you already have an account, skip ahead to whichever of the two sections above applies to you. If not, an account can be created at https://app.datamermaid.org/.
2. API keys
-----------
.. _`API key`:
An API key is a long-lived credential for scripts, notebooks and other machine clients that cannot complete a browser login. A key acts as the user who created it: every request it authenticates has exactly the projects and roles that user has, and loses access the moment a project membership is removed. It does **not** have its own, separate scope — anyone holding the key can do anything its creator's account can do, so treat it like a password and store it accordingly (an environment variable or secret manager, not source control).
Keys are managed at ``/apikeys/`` (see `Non-Project resources`) while signed in with a normal token; creating and revoking a key is the one thing a key cannot be used for itself (see below), so this step always needs a real, browser-based login. Any MERMAID account can create keys for itself; no special role is needed. Creating a key returns the key itself once, in the ``key`` field of the response. It is not stored and cannot be shown again, so copy it straight away. A key expires one year after it is created unless another expiry, or ``never_expires``, is given when it is created.
The key is sent in the same header as a token, and never in the URL:
::
curl --request GET \
--url https://api.datamermaid.org/v1/projects/ \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer mmd_prod_xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx_...'
A key cannot be used to list, create or revoke API keys; that always requires a signed-in user. This means a leaked key cannot be used to issue itself a replacement or extend its own life.

`OAuth2 Implicit grant type`_ is used to fetch a valid token that can be used to securely access MERMAI

title: Mermaid Pricing: Plans for Individuals & Teams
snippet:
### Basic
Free
For getting started and simple diagrams
- 3 Diagrams
- Limited diagram size
- Limited AI
- 1 team & project creation
- Limited workflow runs
### Plus
$10 per user / month
Billed Annually
For individuals who diagram often
- Unlimited diagrams
- Limitless diagram size
- 300 AI credits per year
### Premium
Most Popular
$20 per user / month
Billed Annually
For advanced users and teams running AI workflows
- 500 shared workflow runs per month
- 2,000 AI credits per year
- Unlimited free viewer seats
- Unlimited teams & project creation
### Enterprise
Custom
Billed Annually
For organizations that need scale and control
- SSO
- Custom contract & invoicing
- IP management
- Dedicated Customer Success Manager (CSM)

The Basic plan gives you access to core features so you can start creating diagrams right away. It’s a great way to explore Mermaid before upgrading.
Plus unlocks unlimited diagrams, limitless diagram size, and 300 AI credits. Premium includes everything in Plus, along with 2,000 AI credits, unlimited viewer seats, and 500 shared workflow runs per month.

No. The core Mermaid syntax is always free and open-source. Paid plans add AI features, diagram storage, real-time collaboration, integrations, and security controls.

title: mermaid-cli/building.md at f87dcd0c9049a58ba75eda6d6dc890e2285be850 · mermaid-js/mermaid-cli
snippet:
1. Add a .npmrc file
```
registry=https://registry.npmjs.com/
@mermaid-js:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken="YOUR-TOKEN"
```
Generate the auth token from the github profile page => settings => developer settings => personal access tokens. Click on the button “Generate new token” and check the checkboxes concerning repo and github registry.
